clues.text: I was a shepherd.
I was the second son born to the first human couple.
My brother killed me.
A conversation between God and my brother followed my death.
I brought some of the firstlings of my flock as an offering to Jehovah.
God said that my blood was crying out from the ground.
My death became the basis for the question, "Am I my brother's guardian?"
My brother spoke with me shortly before killing me in a field.
I died before my parents had a third son.
I never spoke a recorded word in Scripture.
A later letter said my brother's works were wicked and mine were righteous.
I was said to be righteous long after I died.
My blood was contrasted with something that speaks in a better way.
My sacrifice was associated with faith centuries after my death.
I was king of Gerar.
God came to me by night in a dream and warned me about the married woman I had taken.
I sent for Sarah and took her after Abraham said she was his sister.
I had not gone near Sarah when God confronted me in my dream.
God said that if I did not return Sarah to Abraham, I would surely die, along with all who are mine.
I returned Sarah to Abraham and gave him sheep, cattle, and male and female servants.
I told Abraham my land was available and he could dwell wherever he pleased.
I told God that I had acted with an honest heart and innocent hands because I believed Sarah was Abraham's sister.
I asked Abraham what his intentions were when he called Sarah his sister.
After Abraham made supplication, God healed me, my wife, and my slave girls.
God said He held me back from sinning and did not allow me to touch Sarah.
God told me Abraham was a prophet who would make supplication for me so that I would keep living.
I asked God, “will you kill a nation that is really innocent?”
I got up early, told my servants about a dream warning, and they became very frightened.
I asked Abraham what sin I had committed against him that he would bring a great sin upon me and my kingdom.
I gave Sarah 1,000 pieces of silver as a sign of her innocence before everybody.
Jehovah had made all the women of my house barren because of Sarah until Abraham prayed.
With Phicol the chief of my army, I asked Abraham to swear he would not deal falsely with me or my descendants.
Abraham complained to me about a well of water that my servants had violently seized.
I told Abraham I did not know who seized a well of water and had heard nothing about it until that day.
After making a covenant at Beer-sheba, Phicol and I returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham offered seven female lambs to me as a witness that he dug the well at Beer-sheba.
I asked Isaac why he had said that his wife was his sister.
I was king of the Philistines in Gerar when Isaac came there during a famine.
Looking out a window, I saw Isaac displaying affection for Rebekah.
I commanded that anybody touching Isaac and Rebekah would surely be put to death.
I told Isaac to move away because he had grown far stronger than my people.
My people filled with soil the wells that Abraham's servants had dug.
After sending Isaac away for growing too strong, I later sought a peaceful oath with him at Beer-sheba.
I came to Isaac from Gerar with Ahuzzath my personal adviser and Phicol the chief of my army.
I told Isaac that Jehovah had clearly been with him, and I sought an oath of obligation and a covenant.
I told Isaac that one of the people could easily have lain down with his wife and brought guilt upon my people.
Isaac asked why I had come, seeing that I had hated him and sent him away.
Isaac prepared a feast for me, and early the next morning I swore an oath with him and sent him away in peace.
Herdsmen from my land quarrelled with Isaac's herdsmen over wells of water.
I became the father of Isaac.
I left Haran when I was seventy-five years old.
I listened to Sarah and had a child through Hagar.
I was called Jehovah's friend.
I was willing to offer my son as a sacrifice.
Jehovah promised that all nations would obtain a blessing through my offspring.
Jehovah told me to leave my country and my relatives.
My wife was my half-sister.
I built altars to Jehovah in the land I was shown.
I gave a tenth of everything to Melchizedek.
I had a son named Ishmael before Isaac was born.
I laughed when told that I would become a father in my old age.
I left Ur before settling in Canaan.
I let Lot choose which part of the land he would take.
I rescued Lot after he was taken captive.
I said, "God himself will provide the sheep for the burnt offering, my son."
I thought my servant Eliezer of Damascus would become my heir.
I was one hundred years old when Isaac was born.
I went down to Egypt because of a famine.
Isaac and Ishmael buried me together.
My name was changed after I was told that I would become the father of many nations.
A deep sleep fell upon me while Jehovah made a covenant concerning my descendants.
Birds of prey came down on the animal pieces, and I drove them away.
I armed trained men born in my household and pursued four kings.
I asked, "O Sovereign Lord Jehovah, what will you give me, seeing that I continue childless?"
I believed Jehovah, and it was counted to me as righteousness.
I cut animals in two when Jehovah made a covenant with me.
I pleaded for a city not to be destroyed if righteous people could be found there.
I prayed, and God healed Abimelech and his household.
I ran to meet three men and had a meal prepared for them.
I refused to keep the goods recovered after defeating a coalition of kings.
I was deeply distressed when Sarah demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away.
Three visitors came to me while I was sitting at the entrance of my tent during the heat of the day.
Twice, I said that my wife was my sister.
A ram caught by its horns in a thicket became part of one of my most important experiences.
A smoking furnace and a fiery torch passed between the pieces of the animals.
After Sarah died, I took another wife, Keturah.
By faith I went out though I did not know where I was going.
Early the next morning I looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and saw dense smoke rising.
I bowed down before the people of the land when negotiating for a burial place.
I buried my wife in a cave of the field of Machpelah.
I chased invading kings as far as Dan.
I died at 175 years of age.
I gave Isaac everything I had, but I sent the sons of my concubines away eastward with gifts.
I made a covenant with Abimelech concerning a well.
I planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba.
I purchased a burial place from the sons of Heth.
I purchased land for 400 silver shekels.
I reasoned that God was able to raise Isaac up even from the dead.
I refused to accept even a thread or a sandal lace from a king.
I sent my servant to find a wife for Isaac from among my relatives.
I stretched out my hand and took a knife to kill my son.
I was ninety-nine years old when I was circumcised.
Animals were brought to me so that I could name them.
I lived in the garden of Eden.
I said, "This is at last bone of my bones And flesh of my flesh."
I was formed from the dust of the ground.
I was the first man.
I was told not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and bad.
My wife gave me some fruit from a tree we had been commanded not to eat from, and I began eating it.
I became the husband of the first woman.
I cultivated and cared for a garden that Jehovah God planted.
I gave my wife her name because she would become the mother of everyone living.
I heard Jehovah's voice and hid myself.
I received the breath of life directly from Jehovah.
I became a father to Cain, Abel, and Seth.
I said, "The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree."
I sewed fig leaves together to make coverings for myself and my wife.
I was put into a deep sleep before my wife was created.
I was told, "By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground."
The ground was cursed on my account.
Cherubs and a flaming blade appeared after I lost my home.
Death spread to all mankind through what I did.
I became a father at 130 years of age.
I became a living person, but another man was later called a life-giving spirit.
I lived for 930 years.
I met my wife for the first time after waking up from sleep.
I was described as a pattern of the one who was to come.
My son murdered his own brother.
My wife was deceived, but I was not.
The first woman was built from something taken from me.
Through one act of disobedience by me, many were constituted sinners.
I bore Joseph two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
My two sons were born before the years of famine began in Egypt.
Pharaoh gave me to Joseph as a wife.
I was the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On.
Jacob gave my two sons a place among his own sons.
My husband helped save Egypt from starvation during a famine.
My son Ephraim received the greater blessing from Jacob.
I was the youngest son of my father's favorite wife.
Joseph was my brother.
My mother died shortly after giving birth to me.
I was one of the twelve sons of Jacob.
My father was especially protective of me after Joseph disappeared.
My mother named me while she was dying.
My father gave me a different name than the one my mother chose.
I traveled to Egypt during a famine with my brothers.
Joseph wept after seeing me again.
I received five times as much food as my brothers at a banquet.
A silver cup was secretly placed in my sack.
My brothers tore their garments after something was discovered in my belongings.
Judah offered himself as a slave because of what happened to me.
I was born on the journey between Bethel and Ephrath.
My full brother was Joseph.
I was falsely accused of stealing.
My mother called me "Son of My Mourning."
I was the only one of Joseph's brothers who was not involved in selling him into slavery.
I had ten sons.
My descendant was the first king of Israel.
My father said that I would keep on tearing prey to pieces like a wolf.
I killed my brother.
I was the first son born to Adam and Eve.
I was a cultivator of the ground.
My offering did not receive the same favor as my brother's offering.
I asked, "Am I my brother's guardian?"
I presented some of the produce of the ground as an offering.
Jehovah warned me that sin was crouching at the door.
I spoke with my brother before killing him in a field.
My brother's blood became evidence against me.
I was cursed from the ground that had received my brother's blood.
I said, "My punishment for my error is too great to bear."
I became a wanderer and a fugitive.
I feared that someone finding me would kill me.
Jehovah placed a sign for me after I expressed fear for my life.
I settled in the land of Nod east of Eden.
I built a city and named it after my son.
My son's name was Enoch.
I went away from before Jehovah.
The first recorded murder in Scripture was committed by me.
A warning about mastering sin was given to me before I committed my most famous act.
My descendant Lamech became known for a violent boast.
My family line included people associated with tents, livestock, music, and metalworking.
I was a daughter of Jacob and Leah.
I went out to spend time with the young women of the land.
Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, violated me.
I was among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob.
Jacob later condemned Simeon and Levi's violence that followed what was done to me.
My brothers required the men of Shechem to be circumcised before they would agree to give me in marriage.
Shechem wanted me as his wife after violating me.
Simeon and Levi took me from Shechem's house after killing Shechem and Hamor.
All my days amounted to 365 years.
I walked with the true God for 300 years after becoming father to my son.
I was the father of Methuselah.
God took me, and I was no more.
I prophesied that Jehovah would come with his holy myriads to execute judgment.
I received witness that I had pleased God.
I was the seventh in line from Adam.
The writer of Hebrews listed me among people of faith.
I was Jacob's twin brother.
I sold my birthright for a meal.
I was a skillful hunter.
Isaac loved me because he enjoyed eating wild game that I provided.
I was given another name tied to the red stew I traded for.
I came out of the womb before my brother.
My body was described as being like a garment of hair when I was born.
I asked for some of a red stew when I returned exhausted from the field.
I despised my birthright.
My father intended to bless me before my brother intervened.
I cried out with a loud and bitter cry after losing a blessing.
I said, "Is he not rightly named Jacob?"
I planned to kill my brother after my father died.
I married Judith and Basemath, bringing bitterness to my parents.
I moved to the mountainous region of Seir.
I met my returning brother with four hundred men.
I ran to meet my brother, embraced him, and kissed him.
I refused a gift at first because I already had many possessions.
My descendants became known as the Edomites.
I was forty years old when I married two Hittite women.
I took a daughter of Ishmael as a wife after seeing that my parents disapproved of my earlier marriages.
Later writings used me as an example of someone who gave up something valuable for immediate gratification.
I sought a blessing with tears after losing it.
I was the first woman.
I was Adam's wife.
A serpent spoke to me in the garden of Eden.
I ate fruit from a tree that God had forbidden us to eat from.
I became the mother of all living.
I was made from one of Adam's ribs.
I was created as a helper and complement for Adam.
I saw that a certain tree was good for food and desirable to the eyes.
I gave some fruit to my husband after eating it myself.
I spoke with the serpent before eating the forbidden fruit.
I said, "We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden."
I said, "God has said, 'You must not eat from it, no, you must not touch it; otherwise you will die.'"
After I ate, the eyes of both my husband and me were opened.
My husband and I made coverings from fig leaves.
I heard Jehovah God in the garden after disobeying him.
I was told that childbirth would involve increased pain.
I was told that my husband would dominate me.
I said, "I have produced a man with the help of Jehovah."
I became the mother of Cain and Abel.
I later gave birth to Seth after losing Abel.
I said, "God has appointed for me another offspring in place of Abel."
My husband gave me my name.
A later inspired writer said that I was thoroughly deceived.
Abraham had a son through me.
An angel spoke to me in the wilderness.
I became the mother of Ishmael.
I fled into the wilderness after difficulties arose between Sarah and me.
I was Sarah's servant.
An angel told me to return to my mistress and humble myself.
I became pregnant after Sarah gave me to Abraham.
I began to look down on my mistress after I became pregnant.
I was an Egyptian woman mentioned by name in the Bible.
I was told that my son would be named Ishmael.
I said, "Have I really seen here the One who sees me?"
I wandered in the wilderness of Beer-sheba.
I was sent away with bread and a skin bottle of water.
Sarah saw my son poking fun at her son and demanded that we be sent away.
A later inspired letter used me to illustrate one of two covenants.
A well was named Beer-lahai-roi because of an experience I had with Jehovah's angel.
God opened my eyes to see a well of water.
I obtained an Egyptian wife for my son.
I placed my son under a bush because I did not want to watch him die.
I sat some distance away and wept while expecting my son's death.
My son became an archer in the wilderness.
My son was described in a later inspired letter as being born through natural descent.
I entered the ark with my wife, my father, and my brothers.
My descendants included Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
My grandson was Nimrod.
I saw my father's nakedness and told my two brothers.
My brothers walked backward with a garment on their shoulders.
An incident involving my father led to a curse being pronounced on Canaan.
I was referred to as "the father of Canaan" while an account about Noah was being told.
My family line included several peoples later associated with Egypt.
The Philistines were listed among peoples descended from my family line.
Many of the nations later living in Canaan traced their ancestry through my descendants.
I was the grandfather of someone who was called a mighty hunter before Jehovah.
The record identifies me as the youngest son involved in an incident after Noah drank wine.
My descendants were grouped separately from those of Shem and Japheth in the Table of Nations.
Abraham was my father.
I married Rebekah.
I was the son whom Abraham was willing to offer as a sacrifice.
Jacob and Esau were my sons.
My mother was Sarah.
A ram took my place on an altar.
I asked my father, “Where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”
I carried the wood for the burnt offering as my father and I went up the mountain.
I loved Esau, but Rebekah favored Jacob.
I met my future wife while I was out walking in a field.
I was born when my parents were very old.
I was circumcised when I was eight days old.
I was comforted after my mother's death when I took Rebekah as my wife.
I was forty years old when I married Rebekah.
My father sent a servant to find a wife for me.
A Philistine king observed me showing affection to my wife.
Abimelech asked me to move away because I had become much mightier than his people.
Before blessing my older son, I asked him to hunt game and prepare a tasty dish for me.
During a famine Jehovah told me not to go down to Egypt.
I became very wealthy in the land of the Philistines.
I prayed concerning my wife because she was barren.
I reopened wells that had been dug in my father's days.
I said that my wife was my sister.
I sowed seed during a famine and reaped a hundredfold.
I was meditating in the field when I looked up and saw the camels coming.
I was sixty years old when my twin sons were born.
Jehovah answered my prayer, and my wife conceived twins.
A later inspired writer used me as an example of a child born through promise.
By faith I blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
Esau's Hittite wives were a source of bitterness to me and Rebekah.
I built an altar and pitched my tent at Beer-sheba.
I grew dim-eyed in my old age.
I lived for 180 years.
I made a covenant with Abimelech after previous tensions.
I named wells Esek, Sitnah, and Rehoboth.
I said, "Now Jehovah has made room for us."
I sent Jacob to Paddan-aram to take a wife from his mother's family.
I trembled violently after learning that I had blessed the wrong son.
Jacob and Esau buried me together.
Jehovah appeared to me at Beer-sheba.
My hands were touched by someone pretending to be Esau.
My mother was Hagar.
I was born before Isaac.
An angel announced my name before I was born.
Isaac and I buried our father together.
I was circumcised when I was thirteen years old.
God promised that I would become a great nation.
My mother and I were sent away into the wilderness.
I was with my mother when a well of water was revealed in the wilderness.
I lived in the wilderness of Paran.
I became an archer.
I was born when Abraham was eighty-six years old.
I was fourteen years older than Isaac.
My mother obtained an Egyptian wife for me.
It was foretold that my hand would be against everyone and everyone's hand against me.
A later inspired letter contrasted my birth with that of Isaac.
I was present when Abraham was buried.
I was mocking my half-brother and his mother kept noticing it.
I was described as becoming a wild donkey of a man.
I fathered twelve chieftains.
My descendants settled from Havilah to Shur near Egypt.
I lived for 137 years.
A later inspired letter referred to me as being born through natural descent.
A later inspired letter associated me with the persecution of one born through spirit.
My name means 'God hears,' reflecting what God heard concerning my mother's affliction.
After I wrestled at Peniel, my name was changed.
At birth I was holding my brother's heel.
Esau was my twin brother.
I loved Rachel.
I obtained my brother's birthright.
I received the blessing that Isaac intended to give to Esau.
I was the father of the twelve tribes.
My daughter Dinah was violated in the land of Canaan.
I dreamed of a stairway reaching from earth to heaven.
I fled from my brother.
I named that place Bethel.
I rolled the stone from a well's mouth so Rachel's flock could drink.
I said that the scepter would not depart from Judah.
I said, "Surely Jehovah is in this place and I did not know it."
I set up the stone I had used as a pillow and poured oil on top of it.
I spent the night with a stone serving as my pillow.
I was given Leah instead of Rachel on my wedding night.
I worked seven years to marry Rachel.
When I first met Rachel, I kissed her and burst into tears.
A man touched my hip socket during an all-night struggle.
Before meeting Esau, I divided the people with me into two camps.
I became the father of Joseph.
I erected a stone pillar as a witness to a covenant with Laban.
I made an agreement with Laban that involved striped, speckled, and spotted livestock.
I named the place Peniel because I had seen God face to face and yet my life was preserved.
I prayed that Jehovah would save me from my brother's hand.
I rebuked Simeon and Levi for making me a stench to the inhabitants of the land.
I said, "I will not let you go until you bless me."
I secretly left Laban's household and headed toward Canaan.
I sent gifts ahead of me because I feared meeting my brother.
I told Laban he had changed my wages ten times.
I vowed that if God was with me, I would give him a tenth of all he gave me.
I wrestled through the night with a man.
The first seven years I worked for Rachel seemed like only a few days because of my love for her.
I believed that a wild animal had torn Joseph to pieces.
I blessed Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.
I bought a tract of land near Shechem for one hundred pieces of money.
I built booths for my livestock and called the place Succoth.
I buried foreign gods beneath a big tree near Shechem.
I crossed my hands while blessing two grandsons.
I described Judah as a lion cub.
I died in Egypt at 147 years of age.
I hesitated to send Benjamin to Egypt.
I learned that my son was still alive after believing he was dead for many years.
I limped after an encounter that changed my name.
I made Joseph swear not to bury me in Egypt but with my fathers.
I met my brother again after many years, and he embraced me.
I moved my household to Egypt during a famine.
I refused to be comforted after losing a beloved son.
I said I never expected to see Joseph's face again, yet God let me see his sons as well.
I sent my sons to Egypt during a famine.
I told Pharaoh that my years had been few and distressing.
My body was carried back to Canaan for burial.
My wife Rachel died while giving birth to Benjamin.
While dying, I worshiped as I leaned on the top of my staff.
I was one of Noah's sons.
I survived the Flood aboard the ark along with my parents and brothers.
Shem and Ham were my brothers.
I entered the ark with my wife and family.
I was among the eight humans who survived the Flood.
My brother and I walked backward with a garment to cover our father.
A blessing spoken by Noah included me after an incident involving wine.
Noah prayed that God would grant ample space to me.
It was foretold that I would reside in the tents of Shem.
My descendants included Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
My family line is listed first among Noah's descendants in the Table of Nations.
The coastland peoples were listed among descendants of my family line.
My descendants spread by their lands, languages, families, and nations.
A later genealogy traced many nations through my descendants.
I was present when the post-Flood world began to be repopulated.
I became a powerful ruler in Egypt.
I interpreted Pharaoh's dreams.
I received a special robe from my father.
I was Jacob's favorite son.
I was thrown into a pit by my brothers.
My brothers bowed down before me.
My brothers sold me into slavery.
I brought a bad report about my brothers to my father.
I dreamed that sheaves belonging to my brothers bowed down to my sheaf.
I dreamed that the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.
I had dreams that caused my brothers to hate me.
I predicted seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine.
I refused the advances of my master's wife.
I served in the household of Potiphar.
I shocked my brothers when I revealed who I really was.
I was imprisoned for a crime I did not commit.
I was seventeen years old when I was tending flocks with my brothers.
Jehovah made me successful in everything I did in my Egyptian master's house.
My garment was used as false evidence against me.
Before I appeared before Pharaoh, I shaved and changed my clothes.
I accused my brothers of being spies.
I asked a cupbearer to remember me after he was restored to his position.
I bound Simeon before his brothers' eyes until they brought Benjamin.
I interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker.
I married Asenath.
I proposed storing food during the seven years of abundance.
I recognized my brothers when they came to Egypt, but they did not recognize me.
I remained in prison for two more years after a favorable interpretation came true.
I said, "Interpretations belong to God."
I seated my brothers by age, and they looked at one another in amazement.
I served Benjamin five times as much food as his brothers.
I was thirty years old when I entered Pharaoh's service.
My sons were named Manasseh and Ephraim.
Pharaoh gave me authority second only to his own.
A later inspired writer praised my faith regarding Israel's departure from Egypt.
I arranged for a silver cup to be hidden in my brother's sack.
I asked that my bones be carried out of Egypt in the future.
I asked, “Am I in the place of God?” when my brothers feared revenge.
I demanded that my youngest brother be brought to Egypt.
I forgave the brothers who had wronged me.
I lived to be 110 years old.
I provided food for many people during a severe famine.
I said, "You meant to harm me, but God meant it for good."
I secretly returned money to my brothers' sacks.
I settled my father and brothers in the land of Goshen.
I told my brothers that God had sent me ahead of them to preserve lives.
I was embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt.
I wept after seeing my brother Benjamin again.
I wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard me when I made myself known to my brothers.
My bones were eventually buried at Shechem.
My father believed I had been torn to pieces by a wild animal.
I was one of Jacob's sons.
My mother named me while praising Jehovah.
I suggested that my brothers sell one of our brothers instead of killing him.
I helped arrange the sale of my brother to traveling merchants.
A tribe of Israel was named after me.
Kings later came from my family line.
My father compared me to a lion cub.
I left my brothers for a time and associated with an Adullamite named Hirah.
I married the daughter of a Canaanite named Shua.
I had sons named Er, Onan, and Shelah.
Two of my sons died because they were displeasing to Jehovah.
I promised my youngest son to my daughter-in-law but delayed fulfilling that promise.
I unknowingly fathered children through my own daughter-in-law.
I gave my seal ring, cord, and staff as a pledge.
I said, "She is more righteous than I am."
Twin sons were born through a situation that brought me public embarrassment.
I became the spokesman for my brothers during our trips to Egypt.
I guaranteed my youngest brother's safety to our father.
I said, "I will be the one to answer for him."
I persuaded my father to let Benjamin travel with us to Egypt.
I was placed in charge of presenting our case after a silver cup was discovered.
I offered myself as a slave in place of my younger brother.
My plea moved a powerful Egyptian ruler to tears.
I did not realize that the ruler of Egypt was my brother when I spoke in his defense.
I approached an Egyptian ruler and said, "Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord's hearing."
My descendants camped on the east side of the tabernacle alongside Issachar and Zebulun.
My daughter-in-law sent me my own seal ring, cord, and staff as evidence.
One of my sons failed to provide offspring for his deceased brother and died for it.
I thought a veiled woman by the road was a prostitute.
A friend of mine searched unsuccessfully for a woman to recover items I had pledged.
I was prepared to have someone executed before learning that I shared responsibility for the situation.
Perez and Zerah were among my descendants.
My father declared that the scepter would not depart from my line.
My father said that my brothers would praise me.
My descendants included David and Jesus Christ.
My name became associated with the royal tribe of Israel.
Jacob worked for me in order to marry one of my daughters.
I had two daughters named Leah and Rachel.
I tricked Jacob into marrying my older daughter first.
Jacob ended up serving me for fourteen years to marry both of my daughters.
I was the brother of Rebekah.
Bethuel and I said that the request to take my sister Rebekah as a wife for Abraham's son had come from Jehovah.
I was the father-in-law of Jacob.
I changed Jacob's wages repeatedly.
I met Abraham's servant at a well after hearing about gifts given to my sister.
I welcomed a servant who arrived seeking a wife for his master's son.
I insisted that my older daughter marry before my younger daughter.
My flocks became the subject of an unusual breeding arrangement involving striped rods.
Jacob became wealthy while tending my flocks.
My sons claimed that Jacob had taken everything that belonged to me.
My daughters complained that I had treated them as foreigners.
I pursued Jacob after he secretly departed with my family and possessions.
God warned me in a dream not to speak either good or bad to Jacob.
I accused Jacob of leaving secretly and carrying off my daughters like captives of war.
I searched for household gods that had been stolen from me.
My daughter sat on the stolen household gods while I searched for them.
I never found the household gods that had been taken from me.
Jacob reminded me that he had endured heat by day and cold by night while serving me.
Jacob said that I had changed his wages ten times.
I made a covenant with Jacob and marked it with a heap of stones.
I called a memorial heap by an Aramaic name, while Jacob called it by a Hebrew name.
I said, "May Jehovah keep watch between you and me when we are hidden from each other."
I warned Jacob not to mistreat my daughters or take additional wives besides them.
My son-in-law offered a sacrifice near the boundary marker after we settled our dispute.
I kissed my daughters and grandchildren before returning home.
My father substituted me for my younger sister on a wedding night.
I was the older sister of Rachel.
Jacob worked seven years expecting to marry my sister but married me first.
I became one of Jacob's wives.
I was the mother of Judah.
I gave birth to six of Jacob's sons.
Jehovah saw that I was unloved and opened my womb.
My sister remained childless while I gave birth repeatedly.
I named my firstborn Reuben.
I said, "Because Jehovah has looked upon my affliction."
I named a son Simeon because Jehovah had heard that I was unloved.
I named a son Levi because I hoped my husband would become attached to me.
I named a son while saying, "This time I will praise Jehovah."
I temporarily stopped bearing children after the birth of Judah.
I became my husband's first wife through a deception arranged by my father.
My servant Zilpah bore children on my behalf.
I gave my servant to Jacob as a wife after I stopped having children.
I received mandrakes from my son and negotiated with my sister over them.
I said that God had rewarded me for giving my servant to my husband.
I named a son Issachar after believing I had received a reward.
I named a son Zebulun because I believed God had given me a good gift.
I became the mother of Dinah.
My sons Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun became founders of tribes of Israel.
I was buried in the cave of Machpelah.
My husband requested to be buried beside me.
I became an ancestress of both Israel's priestly tribe and its royal tribe.
I was one of four women whose sons became the twelve tribes of Israel.
My eyes had no luster.
I was Abraham's nephew.
I lived in Sodom before its destruction.
Angels led me out of a city before Jehovah destroyed it.
My wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.
I escaped the destruction of Sodom.
I traveled with Abraham from Haran.
My herds became so numerous that the land could not support both me and Abraham together.
I chose the well-watered district of the Jordan when separating from Abraham.
I pitched my tents near Sodom.
I was captured during a war involving several kings.
Abraham rescued me after I was taken captive.
I sat in the gate of Sodom.
I invited two angelic visitors into my home and urged them not to spend the night in the public square.
A violent mob surrounded my house and demanded my guests.
I pleaded with wicked men not to act perversely.
The men of Sodom threatened me after I tried to restrain them.
My sons-in-law thought I was joking when I warned them to flee.
I hesitated when told to flee, and angels took hold of my hand to lead me out.
I asked to flee to a small city instead of the mountains.
I was allowed to flee to a small city, and that city was spared.
I lived in Zoar after escaping judgment.
Later I left Zoar and lived in a cave with my daughters.
My daughters believed there were no men left to preserve our family line.
I became intoxicated on consecutive nights without knowing what followed.
Through my daughters I became the ancestor of two neighboring nations.
Moab and Ben-ammi were born through a tragic episode involving my family.
A later inspired writer described me as distressed by the lawless deeds of wicked people around me.
I was rescued from destruction because God remembered Abraham.
Angels led me out of Sodom with Lot and our two daughters.
I became a pillar of salt.
I began to look back while I was behind Lot.
I was told not to look behind me while escaping.
Jesus told his followers to remember me.
I met Abraham after his victory over several kings.
I was a priest of the Most High God.
I was king of Salem.
I blessed Abraham after his military victory.
I brought out bread and wine for Abraham.
I praised the Most High God for delivering Abraham's enemies into his hand.
I said, "Blessed be Abram by the Most High God, Maker of heaven and earth."
A later inspired writer also associated me with the title "King of Peace."
A later inspired writer explained that my name means "King of Righteousness."
A psalm later foretold a priest who would serve according to the pattern of my priesthood.
Abraham gave me a tenth of the chief spoils.
My brief appearance in Genesis becomes the basis for an extended discussion of my priesthood in Hebrews.
A later writer said that even Levi, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham when Abraham gave me a tenth.
I was described as being "made like the Son of God."
Levi was still a future descendant of his forefather, when I met Abraham.
The Scriptural account does not record my father, mother, genealogy, beginning of days, or end of life.
I became a mighty hunter in opposition to Jehovah.
I became the first mighty one on the earth after the Flood.
I was a grandson of Ham.
My kingdom began with Babel.
I built Nineveh.
Although my account spans only a few verses, I was remembered for both hunting and kingdom-building.
I was a son of Cush.
My account appears immediately before the Bible explains why mankind's languages were confused.
My reputation as a hunter became proverbial.
The Bible introduces me as a kingdom builder soon after describing the descendants of Noah.
The beginning of my kingdom included Erech, Accad, and Calneh.
A later prophet spoke of my land together with the land of Assyria.
I also built Rehoboth-Ir and Calah.
Out of the land where my kingdom began, I went forth into Assyria.
Resen, between Nineveh and Calah, was called the great city in connection with my building.
I built an ark.
I survived the Flood with my family.
I found favor in Jehovah's eyes.
I was a righteous man who walked with the true God.
I became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
I obeyed everything Jehovah commanded me to do.
Jehovah established a covenant with me and my descendants after the Flood.
The rainbow became the sign of the covenant Jehovah made with me.
Jehovah told me to be fruitful and become many.
Pairs of animals entered the ark with me, as Jehovah had instructed.
I also brought groups of clean animals into the ark.
Jehovah shut the door of the ark after I entered.
I witnessed rain fall for forty days and forty nights.
I remained in the ark while the floodwaters prevailed for one hundred and fifty days.
Jehovah remembered me while I was in the ark.
The ark carrying my family came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
After the Flood, I was permitted to eat animal flesh.
Jehovah told me not to eat flesh with its blood still in it.
Jehovah told me that human lifeblood must be accounted for.
I became a cultivator of the ground and planted a vineyard.
I drank wine from my vineyard and became intoxicated.
The nations after the Flood descended from my three sons.
I released a raven after the Flood.
I released a dove three times to learn whether the waters had receded.
A dove returned to me carrying a freshly plucked olive leaf.
The third time I released a dove, it did not return to me.
I removed the covering of the ark and looked upon the ground.
I remained in the ark until Jehovah instructed me to come out.
I offered clean animals and clean birds as burnt offerings after the Flood.
I lay uncovered inside my tent after becoming drunk.
One of my sons saw my nakedness and told his two brothers.
Two of my sons walked backward with a garment on their shoulders so they would not see my nakedness.
When I awoke from my wine, I learned what my youngest son had done.
I pronounced a curse upon Canaan.
I said, "Praised be Jehovah, the God of Shem."
I declared that God would grant ample space to Japheth.
Jehovah smelled a pleasing aroma after I offered sacrifices.
Jehovah promised me that seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night would never cease while the earth remains.
Jehovah included every living creature with me in the covenant He established after the Flood.
I foretold that Japheth would reside in the tents of Shem.
I lived for three hundred and fifty years after the Flood.
I lived to be nine hundred and fifty years old.
A later inspired writer called me "a preacher of righteousness."
By faith I built an ark for the saving of my household.
By my faith I condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that results from faith.
Jesus compared the days before the Flood of my time to the period before his presence.
I dreamed of seven fine-looking, fat cows coming up from the Nile.
I invited Joseph's father and households to come to Egypt and eat the richest part of the land.
I put Joseph over all the land of Egypt.
In my dream, seven ugly, thin cows ate up the seven fat cows.
Joseph interpreted my dreams as seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine.
When Egyptians cried to me for bread, I told them to go to Joseph.
Egypt's magic-practicing priests and wise men could not interpret my dreams.
I asked Jacob how old he was.
I asked Joseph's brothers, “What is your occupation?”
I asked my servants whether another man could be found like Joseph, in whom there was the spirit of God.
I clothed Joseph with garments of fine linen and placed a necklace of gold around his neck.
I dreamed of seven full ears of grain on one stalk, then seven thin ears scorched by the east wind.
I gave Joseph Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera the priest of On, as a wife.
I gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah.
I had Joseph ride in the second chariot of honor that I had.
I removed my signet ring from my hand and put it on Joseph's hand.
I sent for Joseph and had him brought quickly from prison.
I told Joseph that only as to the throne would I be greater than he was.
In my dream, the thin ears of grain swallowed up the full, choice ears.
My chief cupbearer told me about a young Hebrew who had interpreted prison dreams correctly.
I commanded that wagons be taken from Egypt to bring Joseph's father and households down.
I grew indignant at my chief cupbearer and chief baker and committed them to the jail of the chief of the guard.
I said I had never seen such bad-looking cows in all the land of Egypt.
I said that if Joseph knew of any capable men among his brothers, he should put them in charge of my livestock.
I told Joseph not to worry about his family's belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt was theirs.
I told Joseph that without his authorization no man may do a single thing in all the land of Egypt.
I told Joseph to settle his father and brothers in Goshen, the very best part of the land.
In my dream, after the thin cows ate the fat ones, they still looked just as bad as at the start.
In the morning after my dreams, my spirit became agitated.
Jacob blessed me when Joseph presented him, and he blessed me again before leaving.
Joseph bought all the Egyptians' land for me, except the land of the priests.
Joseph kept bringing into my house the money collected for grain sold in Egypt and Canaan.
Joseph made a decree over Egypt that a fifth of the produce belongs to me, and that decree remained valid.
On my birthday I made a feast for all my servants, restored the chief cupbearer, and hanged the chief baker.
People were to call out “Avrekh!” ahead of Joseph after I elevated him.
A later psalm said that I sent to release Joseph and made him master of my household and ruler over all my property.
After two full years, dreams of cows and grain led me to free a Hebrew prisoner and place him over Egypt.
I first jailed my cupbearer in anger, then later learned from him about the Hebrew who could interpret dreams.
I gave Joseph my signet ring and fine linen, then later sent wagons so his family could eat the richest part of Egypt.
I settled Joseph's family in Goshen and afterward asked Jacob his age and received his blessing.
Joseph's storage proposal pleased me, and when famine came I redirected the crying Egyptians to him.
I bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites who had brought him to Egypt.
I was an Egyptian court official and the chief of Pharaoh's guard.
Jehovah blessed my house for Joseph's sake.
Jehovah made everything Joseph did in my house successful.
I became furious when I heard my wife's accusation against Joseph.
I put Joseph in charge of my house and everything I had.
I put my slave in the prison where Pharaoh's prisoners were held.
My wife repeatedly urged Joseph to lie down with her.
Once Joseph was overseer, I paid attention to nothing in my house except the bread I ate.
Day after day I spoke to Joseph, but he would not consent.
I told Joseph, “Lie down with me.”
Joseph fled from me and left his garment in my hand.
I began to cast my eyes on Joseph while he served in my husband's house.
Joseph told me that lying with me would be a great badness and a sin against God.
When none of the household servants were in the house, I grabbed Joseph by his garment.
After Joseph fled, I cried out to the men of my house.
I accused Joseph of coming to make me a laughingstock.
I laid Joseph's garment beside me until my husband came to his house.
I told my husband that his Hebrew servant had come to make me a laughingstock.
I claimed that as soon as I raised my voice and screamed, Joseph left his garment and fled outside.
I told the men of my house that a Hebrew man had been brought in to make me a laughingstock.
My accusation made my husband's anger blaze, and Joseph was put in the prison where the king's prisoners were kept.
Benjamin was my son.
I was the younger daughter of Laban.
Jacob loved me and agreed to work seven years to marry me.
Jacob worked another seven years because of me.
Joseph was my first son.
My father deceived Jacob by giving him my sister instead of me.
I envied my sister because she had children while I remained barren.
I gave my servant Bilhah to my husband so that I could have children through her.
I named Dan and Naphtali.
I said to my husband, "Give me children, or otherwise I will die."
I was a shepherdess when Jacob first met me.
I was beautiful in form and beautiful of face.
Jehovah remembered me and opened my womb.
I died while giving birth to my second son.
I hid the household gods in a camel basket and sat on them.
I secretly took my father's household gods when we left his home.
I traded a night with my husband for some of my nephew's mandrakes.
When my first son was born, I said that God had taken away my reproach.
As I was dying, I named my son Ben-oni.
I told my father I could not stand up because I was experiencing the customary thing with women.
I was buried on the way to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem.
My husband set up a pillar over my grave.
A prophet later used my name when describing mothers weeping for their children.
Abraham's servant met me at a well.
I became Isaac's wife.
I offered water not only to a traveler but also to all of his camels.
I was the mother of Esau and Jacob.
I favored my younger son, while my husband favored the older.
I was barren until Jehovah answered my husband's prayers.
My family asked me whether I was willing to leave with Abraham's servant, and I answered, "I am willing to go."
While I was pregnant, my children struggled within me.
After my older son said he intended to kill his brother, I urged the younger to flee.
I covered my son's hands and neck with goatskins.
I helped my younger son receive his father's blessing.
I inquired of Jehovah when the children struggled within me.
I overheard my husband preparing to bless our older son.
I persuaded my husband to send our younger son to my brother's household.
I prepared a meal so that my younger son could take it to his father.
I said I was disgusted with life because of the Hittite women my older son married.
Jehovah told me "the older would serve the younger."
My brother was Laban.
A man who met me gave me a gold nose ring and bracelets before asking my family for permission to take me away.
Before my marriage, my family blessed me with the wish that my offspring would possess the gate of those hating them.
I told my son to let any curse for deceiving his father come upon me.
My husband loved me and found comfort after the death of his mother.
When I first saw my future husband, I got down from my camel and covered myself with a veil.
I lay with Bilhah, my father's concubine.
I tried to rescue Joseph from my brothers and return him to his father.
I was Jacob's firstborn son.
My father said that with reckless license like waters I should not excel.
My mother was Leah.
During the wheat harvest I found mandrakes in the field and brought them to Leah.
I exclaimed, “The child is gone! And I—what am I going to do?”
I reminded my brothers, “Did I not say to you, 'Do not sin against the child,' but you would not listen?”
I told my brothers not to shed blood, but to throw Joseph into a waterpit in the wilderness.
My mother named me because Jehovah had looked upon her affliction.
When I returned to the waterpit and Joseph was not there, I ripped my garments apart.
Because I defiled my father's bed, the right as firstborn was given to the sons of Joseph.
I told my father he could put my own two sons to death if I did not bring Benjamin back.
My father called me his vigor and the beginning of his generative power, the excellence of dignity and strength.
My father said I had gone up to his bed and profaned his lounge.
My sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
I meant to save Joseph from the waterpit, but later told my brothers that his blood was certainly being asked back.
I offered my sons as security for Benjamin, but my father refused to send him with me.
Though I was the firstborn excellence of dignity and strength, my father said not to excel after I profaned his lounge.
I laughed when I heard that I would have a son in my old age.
I was Abraham's wife.
I was barren for many years before giving birth.
Isaac was my son.
A Christian writer used me as an example of faith because I received power to conceive despite my age.
After my servant conceived, she began to despise me.
I dealt harshly with my servant until she ran away.
I denied laughing when questioned about it.
I gave my servant to my husband so that he could have a child through her.
I was originally called by another name before Jehovah changed it.
Three visitors came while I was in the tent, and I listened from the entrance.
Because of my appearance, I was taken into Pharaoh's house.
I died in Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron.
I said, "God has prepared laughter for me. Everybody hearing about it will laugh with me."
I said, “Who would have said to Abraham that I would nurse children?”
I saw my servant's son making fun of my son and asked that they be sent away.
Jehovah told my husband to listen to my voice regarding our son.
My husband purchased the cave of Machpelah after I died.
Twice my husband claimed that I was his sister.
A king restored me to my husband after learning that I was married.
Abimelech gave my husband a thousand pieces of silver on my account.
Christian women are encouraged to imitate me by doing good and not giving way to fear.
I lived to be 127 years old.
I was the only woman whose age at death is explicitly recorded in the Bible.
God afflicted one king's household and warned another king in a dream after I was taken.
I became father to Enosh when I was 105 years old.
I was born to Adam and Eve after Abel was killed.
My mother said that God had appointed me in place of Abel.
Adam became father to me in his likeness, in his image.
I lived 912 years.
I was listed in Jesus' genealogy.
In my son Enosh's days, people began to call on the name of Jehovah.
My family line led to Noah.
I became an ancestor of Abraham.
I survived the Flood aboard the ark.
I was one of Noah's three sons.
I became an ancestor of Jesus Christ.
I lived another 500 years after becoming the father of my son.
I walked backward with one of my brothers while carrying a garment over my shoulders.
I was 100 years old two years after the Flood when my son was born.
My descendants included Eber.
My father declared that Canaan would become a slave to me.
My father praised Jehovah as my God.
One of my brothers had seven sons, and the other had four sons.
The record calls me the father of all the sons of Eber.
Abraham was the ninth generation in line from me.
Arpachshad was my son.
I was still alive when Sarah died.
When Abraham was born, I was still alive and remained alive for much of his lifetime.
I gave birth to twins named Perez and Zerah.
I was later given in marriage to Onan, Er's brother.
I was married to Er, a son of Judah.
I saw that Shelah had grown up, yet I had not been given to him as a wife.
I used a veil and sat at the entrance of Enaim to conceal my identity from Judah.
Judah left his seal ring, cord, and staff with me as a pledge.
Judah ordered that I be brought out and burned when he heard I was pregnant.
Judah told me to remain a widow in my father's house until his son Shelah grew up.
Judah was going up to Timnah for the sheepshearing when he turned aside to me.
During the birth of my twins, a scarlet thread was tied on Zerah's hand.
I sent Judah his seal ring, cord, and staff to show who had made me pregnant.
Judah said that I was more righteous than he was because he had not given me to his son Shelah.
My son Perez became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.
I was the father of Abraham.
I was the father of Nahor and Haran.
I left Ur of the Chaldeans with part of my family.
My son Haran died during my lifetime.
Lot was my grandson.
Sarai was my daughter-in-law.
My family set out for Canaan but stopped before reaching it.
I died before Abraham departed from Haran.
Joshua later said that my household served other gods.
My grandson became a forefather of both the Moabites and the Ammonites.
I was the eighth generation in line from Shem.
I began the journey to Canaan, but my son completed it without me.
